detailed_results.question: What must be true before starting the Hydraulic Power Unit?
detailed_results.answer:
According to ECN-1042.pdf (Extracted PDF Text), ECN-1042.pdf has document text: [Page 1] Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042
Engineering Change Notice
ECN-1042
ECN Number: ECN-1042
Title: Pressure Sensor Replacement (PS-04 fi PS-04A) and Operating Pressure Update
Effective: Software Revision 3.2
Affected Assembly: Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU)
Status: Released
1. Description of Change
Effective software revision 3.2, pressure sensor PS-04 is replaced by pressure sensor PS-04A at the HPU
discharge line. PS-04A uses an updated signal conditioning circuit and is not a form-fit-function replacement for
PS-04; controller firmware must be at revision 3.2 or later to read PS-04A correctly.
Alongside the sensor change, the normal HPU discharge pressure setpoint is revised from 180 bar to 200 bar.
This is a deliberate process change, not a sensor calibration artifact: the higher setpoint improves press cycle
time on Series-7 units manufactured after 2024.
PS-04 remains installed and supported on units running software revisions prior to 3.2. Do not install PS-04A on
a controller running firmware older than 3.2.
2. Reason for Change
Field data showed PS-04's signal drift exceeded tolerance after approximately 18 months of continuous service
in high-cycle installations, occasionally triggering nuisance Alarm A19 (Sensor Signal Invalid). PS-04A corrects
this drift behavior.
3. Impacted Documentation
Operator Manual AEG-OM-700, Maintenance Manual AEG-MM-700, and Component Register AEG-CR-700
have been updated to reflect PS-04A and the 200 bar setpoint. See also ECN-1058 for a related alarm
threshold correction.

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Operator Manual
Document AEG-OM-700 | Revision 4 | Applies to software revision 3.2 and later
1. Overview
The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS) provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for
industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), which supplies pressurized
fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the HCS Controller (PLC-03).
Throughout Aegis documentation the Hydraulic Power Unit may also be referred to as the Hydraulic Unit or
the HP unit, depending on which department produced the document. All three terms refer to the same
physical assembly.
2. Key Components
Reference Component Function
HPU Hydraulic Power Unit Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure
IV-21 Isolation Valve 21 Isolates the HPU from the press circuit
PS-04A Pressure Sensor 04A Reports HPU discharge pressure to PLC-03
PLC-03 HCS Controller Supervises startup, monitoring, and alarms
Note: earlier Aegis units shipped with pressure sensor PS-04. As of software revision 3.2, PS-04 is superseded by PS-04A; see
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 for details.
4. Operating Procedures
4.3 Starting the Hydraulic Power Unit
Before starting, verify:
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band on the sight glass.
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is OPEN.
(cid:127) The emergency stop circuit is RESET.
WARNING: Do not start the Hydraulic Power Unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Rotating
components inside the HPU housing are exposed when the panel is off.
Startup sequence:
1 Turn the POWER selector to ON.
2 Press START.
3 Verify discharge pressure, as reported by PS-04A, reaches 200 bar. This is the normal operating pressure
for software revision 3.2 and later; see ECN-1042 for the pressure change history.
5. Normal Operating Ranges
Normal HPU discharge pressure is 200 bar on software revision 3.2 and later. On revisions prior to 3.2, normal
discharge pressure was 180 bar, measured by the original PS-04 sensor. Do not compare live readings against
AEG-OM-700 Rev 4 | Page 1
[Page 2] Aegis Series-7 HCS — Operator Manual AEG-OM-700 Rev 4
the 180 bar figure on a unit running revision 3.2 or later — the setpoint changed along with the sensor
replacement.
6. Alarms
See the Aegis Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) for the full alarm list, including alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure
Low), its possible causes, and required operator actions.
7. Controller Reset
Do not reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. Resetting the controller under
pressure can cause an uncommanded valve transition. Bleed pressure below 50 bar first, using the manual
bleed procedure in Section 8, before performing a controller reset.

maintenance_manual.pdf: document_text = [Page 1] Aegis Series-7 HCS — Maintenance Manual AEG-MM-700 Rev 3
Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Maintenance Manual
Document AEG-MM-700 | Revision 3
1. Scope
This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).
3. Controller Reset Conditions
Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.
Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.
4. Alarm A17 Response
Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.
Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).
6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure
If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is low.
(cid:127) Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.
7. Component Access
The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.
9. Related Documents
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 (pressure sensor replacement and setpoint change), ECN-1058 (alarm
threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual,
as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.
AEG-MM-700 Rev 3 | Page 1

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Maintenance Manual
Document AEG-MM-700 | Revision 3
1. Scope
This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).
3. Controller Reset Conditions
Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.
Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.
4. Alarm A17 Response
Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.
Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).
6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure
If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is low.
(cid:127) Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.
7. Component Access
The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Operator Manual
Document AEG-OM-700 | Revision 4 | Applies to software revision 3.2 and later
1. Overview
The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS) provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for
industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), which supplies pressurized
fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the HCS Controller (PLC-03).
Throughout Aegis documentation the Hydraulic Power Unit may also be referred to as the Hydraulic Unit or
the HP unit, depending on which department produced the document. All three terms refer to the same
physical assembly.
2. Key Components
Reference Component Function
HPU Hydraulic Power Unit Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure
IV-21 Isolation Valve 21 Isolates the HPU from the press circuit
PS-04A Pressure Sensor 04A Reports HPU discharge pressure to PLC-03
PLC-03 HCS Controller Supervises startup, monitoring, and alarms
Note: earlier Aegis units shipped with pressure sensor PS-04. As of software revision 3.2, PS-04 is superseded by PS-04A; see
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 for details.
4. Operating Procedures
4.3 Starting the Hydraulic Power Unit
Before starting, verify:
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band on the sight glass.
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is OPEN.
(cid:127) The emergency stop circuit is RESET.
WARNING: Do not start the Hydraulic Power Unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Rotating
components inside the HPU housing are exposed when the panel is off.
Startup sequence:
1 Turn the POWER selector to ON.
2 Press START.
3 Verify discharge pressure, as reported by PS-04A, reaches 200 bar. This is the normal operating pressure
for software revision 3.2 and later; see ECN-1042 for the pressure change history.
5. Normal Operating Ranges
Normal HPU discharge pressure is 200 bar on software revision 3.2 and later. On revisions prior to 3.2, normal
discharge pressure was 180 bar, measured by the original PS-04 sensor. Do not compare live readings against

the 180 bar figure on a unit running revision 3.2 or later — the setpoint changed along with the sensor
replacement.
6. Alarms
See the Aegis Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) for the full alarm list, including alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure
Low), its possible causes, and required operator actions.
7. Controller Reset
Do not reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. Resetting the controller under
pressure can cause an uncommanded valve transition. Bleed pressure below 50 bar first, using the manual
bleed procedure in Section 8, before performing a controller reset.

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Maintenance Manual
Document AEG-MM-700 | Revision 3
1. Scope
This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).
3. Controller Reset Conditions
Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.
Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.
4. Alarm A17 Response
Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.
Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).
6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure
If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is low.
(cid:127) Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.
7. Component Access
The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.
9. Related Documents

threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual,
as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.

Operator Manual
Document AEG-OM-700 | Revision 4 | Applies to software revision 3.2 and later
1. Overview
The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS) provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for
industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), which supplies pressurized
fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the HCS Controller (PLC-03).
Throughout Aegis documentation the Hydraulic Power Unit may also be referred to as the Hydraulic Unit or
the HP unit, depending on which department produced the document. All three terms refer to the same
physical assembly.
2. Key Components
Reference Component Function
HPU Hydraulic Power Unit Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure
IV-21 Isolation Valve 21 Isolates the HPU from the press circuit
PS-04A Pressure Sensor 04A Reports HPU discharge pressure to PLC-03
PLC-03 HCS Controller Supervises startup, monitoring, and alarms
Note: earlier Aegis units shipped with pressure sensor PS-04. As of software revision 3.2, PS-04 is superseded by PS-04A; see
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 for details.
4. Operating Procedures
4.3 Starting the Hydraulic Power Unit
Before starting, verify:
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band on the sight glass.
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is OPEN.
(cid:127) The emergency stop circuit is RESET.
WARNING: Do not start the Hydraulic Power Unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Rotating
components inside the HPU housing are exposed when the panel is off.
Startup sequence:
1 Turn the POWER selector to ON.
2 Press START.
3 Verify discharge pressure, as reported by PS-04A, reaches 200 bar. This is the normal operating pressure
for software revision 3.2 and later; see ECN-1042 for the pressure change history.
5. Normal Operating Ranges
Normal HPU discharge pressure is 200 bar on software revision 3.2 and later. On revisions prior to 3.2, normal
discharge pressure was 180 bar, measured by the original PS-04 sensor. Do not compare live readings against

the 180 bar figure on a unit running revision 3.2 or later — the setpoint changed along with the sensor
replacement.
6. Alarms
See the Aegis Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) for the full alarm list, including alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure
Low), its possible causes, and required operator actions.
7. Controller Reset
Do not reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. Resetting the controller under
pressure can cause an uncommanded valve transition. Bleed pressure below 50 bar first, using the manual
bleed procedure in Section 8, before performing a controller reset.

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System
Maintenance Manual
Document AEG-MM-700 | Revision 3
1. Scope
This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).
3. Controller Reset Conditions
Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.
Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.
4. Alarm A17 Response
Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.
Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).
6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure
If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
(cid:127) Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
(cid:127) Hydraulic fluid level is low.
(cid:127) Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.
7. Component Access
The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.
9. Related Documents
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 (pressure sensor replacement and setpoint change), ECN-1058 (alarm
threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual,
as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.
